intent: Test whether yaw inertia, not sensing or speed, is the remaining limit on the slalom. Narrow the body to 0.08 m (a free yaw-inertia reduction, since body_width only sets the off-track limit, which stays at the 0.06 m floor) and reduce mass to 0.42 kg, keeping the sensor array, wheel radius and track that already produce oval and s-bend completions.
learning: Iteration 5 confirmed that agility moves slalom progress (0.43 to 0.53) without losing oval completions. Next iteration, check: (a) whether slalom max_error drops below 0.06, which would confirm that yaw inertia is the slalom limit; (b) whether steering_oscillation rises above 0.3, which would mean the agility gain has outrun the damping; (c) whether oval completion_time stays near 1.7 s, which would show the lower mass has not cost traction or speed; (d) whether the s-bend completion rate holds at 17/20 or better. Ask the Integrator whether kd or ki needs retuning after the body narrows.
rationale:
Iteration 5 is the best design so far (score 684.9). Oval finishes 20/20 and s-bend 18/20, but slalom still fails in all 20 trials (off_track, progress 0.53, max_error 0.064). Across iterations 3 to 5, every change that made the body more agile (lower mass, shorter body, narrower track) raised slalom progress (0.34, 0.43, 0.53) without hurting the oval, so yaw response on alternating bends is still the limit. Steering oscillation on the s-bend rose only to 0.31 and control_effort fell, so there is room for more agility before damping becomes the problem.

The contract says body_width only enters the off-track limit, max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). At body_width 0.12 m that limit is at its 0.06 m floor, and it stays at the floor for any width down to 0.08 m (0.0325, still under 0.06). So narrowing the body costs no off-track margin. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2 + W^2)/12, so narrowing the body from 0.12 to 0.08 m cuts the W^2 term by about 45%. With body_length at 0.10 m, the combined term drops from 0.0244 to 0.0164, about a third lower. Together with a mass reduction from 0.45 to 0.42 kg, yaw inertia falls from about 0.00092 to about 0.00057, roughly 38% lower.

Changes: body_width 0.12 to 0.08 m (the main lever, since it is the only yaw-inertia term that is free for the off-track limit), mass 0.45 to 0.42 kg, and wheel_track held at 0.115 m so the turn authority per unit of wheel differential does not increase further. Body_length stays at 0.10 m, which is the minimum. Sensors (7 at x = ±0.03 m, y = 0.08 m, 12 mm footprint) and wheel_radius (0.04 m) are unchanged, so the oval and s-bend completions and the Integrator's controller carry over.

Expected result: slalom max_error below 0.06 and slalom progress above 0.6, with oval completion_time near 1.7 s and s-bend completions held at 17 or more of 20. Risk: the more agile body could raise steering_oscillation above 0.3 and need more kd. If the slalom gets worse, the next step is to return wheel_track toward 0.12 m rather than change the body further.
